scope: Independent source and analytic review of the good sixth-free smooth partner slice. The smooth profile is shared across the complete frequency partition and independent of all equality labels and both varying cutoff labels. The actual separate middle equality compensation is retained.
checks: At fixed log Fourier parameters and partner labels the inverse-profile coefficient stays on the inverse ideal, so the longer cutoff times inverse ideal can be grouped in one positive norm without coupling to the equality allocation. The actual conjugated pairing and the shorter h0^2 b_s norm retain their original phases.

The inverse product has physical length O(M_l B) and divisor-bounded coefficient. Exact S-part and good sixth-power peeling preserve all raw fixed values and zeros, including overlap with the residual; the mass per fiber and convergent inverse-root and inverse-cube weights give the stated norm.

The inverse B dyads have maximum scale V/p, with geometric convergence on both sides and the bounded unit case counted directly. The longer factor is sqrt(M_l) times sqrt((p/V) Phi_6(A,L_l# V/p)); every Phi monomial divided by its length scale is nonincreasing.

For V up to D^(3/8), the excess increment is at most v/2 by the two stated affine branches at l=1/2. This gives V^(-1/4), so V=(Nq)^6 yields a convergent absolute sum of (Nq)^(-3/2) for the short projector.

The complementary signed projector is supported only when the actual good sixth-power base exceeds D^(1/16) and is divisor bounded. The existing large-base estimate applies to its normalized selector with the original middle compensation. The short-projector middle term is counted once with the grouped divisor-bounded coefficient, rather than once per q.
limitations: No sharp main-mode estimate, arbitrary additional selector, rational-content intersection, equality-dependent smooth profile, or new mid-divisor exponent is asserted. No old controls were rerun.
